claims.explanation: Torin-1 is a dual mTORC1/mTORC2 ATP-competitive inhibitor, so sensitivity should track with dependence on mTOR-driven cap-dependent translation and on upstream PI3K/AKT pathway activation. Lines with PIK3CA mutations, PTEN loss, or other lesions that hyperactivate PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling are expected to be selectively killed, whereas lines whose survival is driven by RAS/RAF-MEK-ERK or by neuroblastoma/SCLC lineage programs tend to be less affected. The virtual-cell similarity to other mTOR/PI3K inhibitors supports an on-target mTOR-axis mechanism rather than an off-target effect.

features.basis: Activating PI3K mutations hyperactivate AKT-mTORC1 signaling and create dependence on mTOR; enriched in killed lines (HCC1954, HGC27, KYSE70, 253J, VMCUB1 is an exception).
PTEN loss relieves PI3K-AKT-mTOR inhibition; seen in killed lines WM793, ZR751, and others.
Higher mTOR expression should increase dependence on mTORC1/2 signaling and on-target sensitivity.
mTORC1 scaffold RPTOR is required for mTORC1 output; high expression predicts greater pathway dependence.
S6K1 is a key mTORC1 effector for translation reinitiation; high expression marks mTORC1-addicted lines.
eIF3h mediates mTOR/S6K1-dependent translation reinitiation of uORF mRNAs; high expression may increase dependence on mTOR-driven translation.
High AKT1 expression/activity increases mTORC1 signaling and sensitivity to mTOR inhibition.
KRAS-mutant lines (NCIH1573, NCIH1339, TCCPAN2, PK45H, CAL62) are enriched among least-affected lines, suggesting ERK-driven survival bypasses mTOR dependence.
BRAF-mutant melanoma/glioma lines (WM793, IGR37, AM38, HT115) appear in both extremes but several are least affected, consistent with MAPK-driven survival.
NF1 loss activates RAS-MAPK and is seen in several least-affected lines (RD, LCLC103H, CAL62, HT115).
ALK-altered neuroblastoma lines (KELLY, SKNSH) are among least affected, suggesting lineage/ALK-driven survival independent of mTOR.
Neuroblastoma lines (KELLY, SKNSH, KPNSI9S) are least affected; MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma may rely less on mTORC1 for survival.
